answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a refundable bond that is slashed if clones are detected. A lone whisper of a new account is cheap; the bond must harbor enough capital that spinning hundreds of shells costs more than honest work. When a linked cluster is caught, every bond is driven to its nadir and forfeited together, so the operator loses the entire stake instead of discarding one burned wallet and starting over.
